I expect to be able to do those basic functions by simply tapping a button ether on an app or key fob. Those functions have been available for years on key fobs or free apps. reviews.title: Thanks but no thanks
reviews.text:
This app has become incredibly disappointing. It constantly logs me out, so I’m always having to sign back in. Now, on top of that, Mazda wants to charge $10/month just to use basic features like remote start, remote lock, and remote unlock.

These are features that many customers reasonably expect to be included with a modern vehicle, especially after getting a brand-new car. If they’re going to require a subscription, that should be made abundantly clear during the buying process instead of having dealerships set up the app as if these features are included.

Charging a monthly fee after the fact for functions tied to a vehicle you already paid tens of thousands of dollars for feels like a cash grab. Between the constant login issues and the new subscription requirement, this app has gone from convenient to frustrating.

reviews.title: Bad from the ground up.
reviews.text:
Glad to have remote start, and the app has useful features in theory. But from a design and usability standpoint, it falls far short—especially for a commercial product.

Response times are slow, with long delays between actions and confirmation from the vehicle. Status feedback is inconsistent, hard to interpret, and sometimes missing entirely, making it unclear whether commands succeeded.

Controls are poorly designed. Icons lack clarity, and buttons don’t reflect current status. The most important feature—remote start—is flawed: it uses a scrollable selector as both control and indicator, so accidental changes are easy and you can’t reliably tell if the car is running. Combined with delayed updates, this becomes a real usability problem.

The UI prioritizes appearance over function. Excess whitespace forces unnecessary scrolling and tab switching, and key information isn’t easily accessible. Add frequent pop-ups, too many steps for simple actions, and repeated logins, and the experience becomes frustrating.

Overall, this app is slow, unclear, and inefficient—one of the worst-designed apps I use.

The app is extremely unreliable. It often shows incorrect information about whether my car is locked or unlocked, which makes it impossible to trust for basic vehicle security.

Remote start is also inconsistent. Sometimes the car does not start at all, and when it does, it shuts off far too quickly, making the feature barely useful. The app gives little to no feedback about whether a command actually worked.

Overall, the app lacks useful, accurate, real-time information. For something that’s supposed to add convenience and peace of mind, it instead creates uncertainty and frustration. Mazda makes solid vehicles, but this app seriously needs improvement.

The app appears to log you out on a whim, and I have not figured out what triggers it. However, unless I am going back to it within a timeframe measured in minutes I am almost guaranteed to find I have been logged out. 

When I go to log back in, it firstly displays the old interface, which returns an error code when I log in. If I then close it and reopen it the new interface is displayed but I have to go through the logging in process again, and then accept all the T&C again. This is needlessly complicated and symptomatic of an unfinished app.

They piled on to this truly awful stuff by making the app just not remain in your cache. So nearly every single time you open the app you have to spend 20-30 seconds logging in. That doesn’t sound bad until you do it. It’s so unbelievably frustrating. Especially considering they want 120 dollars a year for you to access your remote start.

reviews.title: Certain features don’t work.
reviews.text: Selecting the map icon within the App used to show where the registered vehicle was located.  Now it shows where my vehicle was on 02/12/25.  This bug seems to have been introduced by a recent App update.  Also the feature that shows how many miles to the next service doesn’t work. reviews.title: Fix Bugs
reviews.text: I’m reviewing again because I’m not sure how Mazda can charge $10/mo for an app that only works some of the time. Mazda is the most greedy company I have ever had the displeasure of ruining my life with. They never fixed my brand new car, they aren’t easy to work with and then my $700+/mo isn’t enough for them, they need to squeeze out another $10/mo from me and everyone so that their car can do the things my 2017 Honda can do without an app and without bugs and without paying extra. As soon as I’m able to get rid of this car that does not function the way it should have when they sold it to me - I will be pleased as punch. I will never buy another Mazda or recommend one to another human being. I value my money and these people are predatory and all of what they have to offer is bottom of the barrel. It should be criminal but I guess that’s capitalism for ya. I would love for someone to tell me why no one could fix my brand new car. I would love for someone to tell me why an app that doesn’t work is worth my extra $10/mo. I also love how this just overwrites my old review so won’t be seen as new so others can’t view it without looking into it.
